newsitem.title: DUBAI: SABIC nine-month profit down 30 percent.
newsitem.headline: SABIC nine-month profit down 30 percent.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp said profits for the first nine months of 1996 fell 30 percent to 3.415 billion riyals from 4.896 billion riyals in the same period last year.
The statement attributed the drop to lower international prices for many of its products.

SABIC, which produces about five percent of the world's petrochemicals, said there was a four percent increase in production in the first eight months of 1996 to 14.87 million tonnes versus the same period last year.
The increase in production was coupled with an increase in sales, which reached 11.462 million tonnes by end-August 1996.
There was a 24 percent increase in sales in the local market to 758,000 tonnes.
SABIC, 70 percent owned by the Saudi government, posted a record 6.28 billion riyal profit for the whole of 1995, up from 4.20 billion in 1994.
